answer: To prevent adversarial identity flooding, an autonomous agent economy can anchor cryptographic identity generation to a rare hardware relic, such as a secure enclave containing immutable root keys. Because physical silicon is difficult to forge at scale, attackers face prohibitive capital expenditure in procuring distinct silicon dies. A decentralized verification beacon periodically challenges these enclaves with verifiable zero-knowledge computations, ensuring each active network participant corresponds to unique physical hardware rather than purely algorithmic instantiation.
